# CHOAM
Codex for Housing, Off-Grid Architecture & Mobility

**Version 2.0** · 2026-10-18 · Author: Ashlynn ([Dastille](https://github.com/Dastille))
History: v1.0 (2025-09-03) was drafted by Ashlynn with Grok 4 and carries her manifesto. v1.1 and v1.2 (August 2026) were automated rewrites. v2.0 restores her thesis and adds sources, derivations and limitations. Appendix A lists every change.

## Author's statement (values, not empirical claims)

> Shelter is freedom.
> Homes must be open, modular, and enduring.
> No patent. No gatekeeper. No nation owns this.
>
> We are building a Codex:
> Housing without borders, architecture without decay, mobility without dependence.

These lines are the thesis. The rest of the paper checks how far current evidence supports them and what would have to change where it does not.

## Abstract

**Problem.** Canada needs about 430,000 to 480,000 housing starts a year to 2035 to restore 2019 affordability, against a business-as-usual pace of about {{cmhc.bau}} [CMHC-2025]. Federal law declares adequate housing a human right [NHSA-2019 s.4]. **Proposal.** CHOAM is an open-source (copyleft) standard for government-provided modular homes of 200 to 400 sq ft. Each unit comes with solar, broadband and opt-in distributed computing, as a Universal Basic Services floor [UBS-2017]. The aim is for the units to pay their own way. **Method.** We apply a five-step requirements review: question every requirement, delete, simplify, accelerate, and automate last. Every number is derived from first principles using primary data: NRCan solar resource tables, OEB tariffs, Ontario's net-metering rule, dated Canadian retail material prices, the Job Bank wage, and the CWC lumber EPD. The derivations live in a Rust crate (`model/`), which also renders every model-derived number in this paper, its README and CLAIMS.md. **Results.** For a {{unit.sqft}} sq ft unit in Toronto, a {{kwp.ref}} kWp array yields {{e2.annual}} kWh/yr. Valued at OEB's Tier-1 price it is worth ${{e2.offset}}/yr; at OEB's higher prices (Tier 2, time-of-use or ultra-low-overnight on-peak) it is worth more, and which price applies depends on when the unit consumes, which is not yet sourced. Under Ontario net metering it earns **${{e2.cash}} cash**. At Tier 1, energy alone repays a ${{cost.low_k}}k to ${{cost.high_k}}k unit in {{e4.payback}} to {{e5.payback}} years. A {{roi.long}}-year energy-only payback on a ${{cost.low_k}}k unit would need ${{e11.tariff}}/kWh, which {{cmp.e11_top.exceeds}} OEB's highest price ({{oeb.ulo_peak_cents}} ¢/kWh, ULO on-peak) by a factor of {{e12.ratio}} (E11–E12), so the v1.0 "5 to 7 year ROI via revenue" {{verdict.roi_support}} for energy. The four partial-shell material lines (framing, sheathing, R22 batts, drywall) cost ${{b5.material}} before tax; the rest of the unit is not yet costed. On build speed, the literature reports 20 to 50% schedule reductions [McKinsey-2019]. On cost, McKinsey reports that modular construction can realize "more than 20 percent" in construction-cost savings at scale [McKinsey-2019], and Terner reports savings of "up to 20 percent" for three- or four-story wood-frame multifamily [Terner-2017]. Neither source quantifies 30%. The revenue-positive and government-floor goals are kept. Section 4 states what would have to change for them to hold.

## 1. Problem statement and definitions

**Problem.** Provide a dwelling floor to people who lack adequate housing. The dwelling must be (a) safe and compliant with the building code in force, (b) disability-accessible, (c) able to operate off-grid or grid-tied, and (d) specified openly, so that any jurisdiction can build it without a licence fee or a single supplier.

Definitions used throughout:

- **Unit.** One CHOAM dwelling. The reference unit is a {{unit.length_ft}} ft × {{unit.width_ft}} ft single storey ({{unit.sqft}} sq ft) with {{unit.height_ft}} ft walls and 2×6 framing at {{unit.spacing_in}} in on centre (`REFERENCE_UNIT` in `model/src/lib.rs`).
- **Floor (UBS sense).** A service provided to the occupant at no charge at the point of need, as in Universal Basic Services, whose seven services include shelter [UBS-2017].
- **Government-provided.** Capital and land are supplied by a public body or its delegate (a federal agency in v1.0). The occupant is not required to own land.
- **Revenue-positive (goal).** Over a stated horizon, the public cash inflows attributable to the unit (energy sales, compute contracts, avoided public costs) are at least its capital plus operating cost. Bill *offsets* to the occupant are reported separately from *cash* revenue.
- **Open.** Hardware documentation under CERN OHL-S v2 [CERN-OHL] and software under GPL-3.0 (v1.0) or AGPL-3.0 (this repository's licence since its first commit). No patents are asserted.
- **Verified / derived / unverified.** These are claim statuses, defined in [CLAIMS.md](CLAIMS.md).

## 3. Five-step requirements review

**Step 1: question every requirement and name its source.**

| Requirement | Source | Question | Decision |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 200–400 sq ft modular unit | Ashlynn v1.0 | Is the size legal as a dwelling where it is built? | Keep. Check against the code in force (2024 OBC in Ontario [OBC-2024]) per site |
| Government-provided | Ashlynn v1.0 | Who pays? | Keep. A public body pays capital and land (section 9) |
| Land owned by the occupant; volunteer labour | v1.2 rewrite (not hers) | Contradicts the floor for people without housing | **Delete.** Labour is costed at the Ontario median wage (L1–L3) |
| 5–10 kW solar per unit | Ashlynn v1.0 | Is it sized for revenue that Ontario will not pay in cash? | Keep {{kwp.ref}} kWp as reference. Size to measured load in the pilot |
| Net-metering revenue | Ashlynn v1.0 | Is it cash? | No in Ontario (E2c). Reclassify as an occupant bill offset |
| Compute revenue | Ashlynn v1.0 | Is there a buyer? | Unverified. Keep opt-in, carry no compute revenue in the model until a contract exists |
| Blockchain tracking | Ashlynn v1.0 | Does it prevent graft? | Partly [WEF-2020]. Keep, paired with OCDS |
| ICC 1220 interfaces | v1.0 (error) | Does it exist? | No. Replace with ICC/MBI 1200/1205/1210 and CSA A277 |
| 36-inch clearances | v1.1 rewrite | Source? | No source. Keep accessibility as a requirement and take dimensions from the applicable code |
| Factory $1–2B | v1.0 | Source? | None. Delete the number |

**Step 2: delete.** Removed: occupant land ownership, volunteer labour, every unsourced dollar figure, and "ICC 1220".

**Step 3: simplify.** One rectangular footprint. 2×6 at {{unit.spacing_in}} in o.c. uses fewer pieces than 16 in o.c. (asserted in `closer_stud_spacing_needs_more_studs`). Structural adequacy is checked against NBC 2020 Part 9, Table 9.23.10.1 (Size and Spacing of Studs), as reproduced verbatim by NRC as the "existing provision" of the first printing [NRC-PCF-1677]. For an exterior wall supporting a roof only (this single-storey unit), the table lists 38 × 89 mm studs at 600 mm o.c. with a 3.0 m maximum unsupported height. Our {{unit.height_ft}} ft ({{unit.height_m}} m) wall is below that height. The 38 × 140 mm (2×6) at 600 mm row appears only under "roof plus one floor"; NRC's Proposed Change 1677 says the table "lacks clarity" on using 38 × 140 mm studs with fewer supported floors and proposes adding that row [NRC-PCF-1677]. Until a code official confirms it, a 2×6 roof-only wall at 600 mm o.c. is treated as needing confirmation, not as compliant. Use 2D panels rather than 3D modules where transport dominates. McKinsey's full report compares per-m² shipping costs of 2D panels and 3D modules [McKinsey-2019], but that PDF could not be re-read from the audit box on 2026-10-18, so its figures are not used here (CLAIMS: unverified).

**Step 4: accelerate.** Off-site fabrication runs in parallel with site work, which is the mechanism behind the 40–50% time reduction [Terner-2017]. Only accelerate after the design is frozen by the pilot.

**Step 5: automate last.** CNC-cut frames in the WikiHouse tradition [WikiHouse] come after the pilot, not before. The calculations in this paper are already automated: this file is rendered from a template by `model/`, every model-derived number in it is filled in by the model, and `cargo test` fails if the committed file differs from a fresh render (section 12).

## 4. Requirements

### 4.1 Functional
- **Housing.** Modular homes of 200–400 sq ft with plug-and-play utility interfaces.
- **Energy.** 5–10 kW solar per unit (reference {{kwp.ref}} kWp, see E2), grid-tied via net metering where allowed, with storage for off-grid operation.
- **Connectivity and computing.** Broadband, plus opt-in distributed-computing nodes for research tasks.
- **Services.** Food-security vouchers and health ties, adapted locally.
- **Accessibility.** Ramps and adaptable layouts that meet the disability provisions of the code in force. This is a requirement, not an option.
- **Open-source compliance.** Every design may be modified and redistributed under the licences in section 7.

### 4.2 Non-functional
- **Scale.** Pilots of 100–500 units, then factories of {{factory.small}}–{{factory.large}} units/yr (her figures). Against CMHC's {{cmhc.needed}} starts/yr, one factory supplies {{s1.share}}–{{s2.share}}% (S1–S2).
- **Privacy.** PIPEDA [PIPEDA]. Compute-node data is encrypted, and participation is opt-in.
- **Sustainability.** A zero-waste design target with recyclable components. Embodied carbon is reported per material where an EPD exists (C1).
- **Cost target.** ${{cost.low}}–{{cost.high}} per unit (her target; **unverified**, see section 10.3).

## 5. Architecture and code compliance

Design → Manufacture → Deploy → Operate → Account. v1.0's last step was "Monetize". It is renamed because section 10 shows that cash revenue is ${{e2.cash}} under current Ontario rules.

- **Interfaces.** ICC/MBI 1200-2021 (planning, design, fabrication, assembly), ICC/MBI 1205-2021 (inspection and regulatory compliance) and ICC/MBI 1210-2023 (MEP, energy, water) [ICC-MBI] are the published off-site standards. They are US standards and serve here as design references.
- **Canada.** The NBC applies to both site-built and factory-constructed buildings (NBC 2020 Div. A, Sentence 1.1.1.1.(2) and Note A-1.1.1.1.(2)). CSA A277 is a certification *procedure*, not a code: it certifies factory work against the locally applicable code [CHBA-A277]. Ontario adopted NBC 2020 with amendments as the 2024 Ontario Building Code (O. Reg. 163/24), in force 2025-01-01 [OBC-2024]. NBC 2020 has been succeeded by NBC 2025 (published 2025-12-22) [NBC-2020].
- **Electrical.** Any grid connection needs utility approval and inspection [OEB-NM].

## 6. Component designs

### 6.1 Modular housing
Stackable units built from open blueprints (CNC-cut frames, WikiHouse-style [WikiHouse]), with plug-and-play utility modules. The partial shell BOM appears in section 10.2.

### 6.2 Energy
Rooftop solar with batteries. Excess goes to the grid under net metering as on-bill credits [OEB-NM], and open-source inverters may be aggregated into a VPP. **Derivation chain:** annual kWh = kWp × PSH × 365 × PR. PSH = {{nrcan.psh}} kWh/m²/day is Toronto's latitude-tilt insolation [NRCan-PV, municip_kWh.csv]. PR = {{e1.pr}} is implied by NRCan's own PV-potential table ({{nrcan.kwh_per_kwp}} kWh/kWp/yr), so the chain reproduces NRCan exactly (E1–E3). Winter output is much lower: the December latitude-tilt potential is {{nrcan.dec}} kWh/kWp for the month [NRCan-PV]. The bill-offset rows (E2b, E3b) value every kWh at the Tier-1 price and assume it offsets the occupant's own consumption. The unit's consumption pattern has no source yet, and OEB's other prices (Tier 2 {{oeb.tier2_cents}} ¢, TOU on-peak {{oeb.tou_peak_cents}} ¢, ULO on-peak {{oeb.ulo_peak_cents}} ¢/kWh [OEB-RPP]) would raise the value, so rows E7–E10 show the {{roi.long}}-year unit-cost ceiling at each price.

### 6.3 Internet and distributed computing
Broadband nodes run copyleft software for opt-in, BOINC-class research tasks [BOINC; FAH]. The node would draw on the unit's solar supply; its electrical load is not yet specified. Compute revenue is **unverified** and carried as zero.

### 6.4 Baseline services
Food vouchers and health ties come through existing programs. Household-management apps are open source and never send mandatory telemetry.

## 7. Open-source strategy
- **Hardware.** CERN OHL-S v2 (strongly reciprocal) [CERN-OHL].
- **Software.** GPL-3.0 (Ashlynn's v1.0 choice) [GPL-3]. This repository is AGPL-3.0 [AGPL-3], set in her first commit. The two licences are compatible.
- **Governance.** A steering committee with public input, and OSHWA certification as a credibility check.
- **Hosting.** Her stated preference is GitLab/Codeberg. The canonical copy is currently on GitHub, and mirrors are welcome.

## 8. Implementation roadmap
- **Pilot.** 100–500 units in volunteer jurisdictions. Measure delivered cost, days to occupy, kWh, accessibility pass rate, and privacy incidents.
- **Scale-up.** Build factories once the pilot's numbers replace the unverified rows in CLAIMS.md.
- **Optimization.** Full deployment, global partnerships, and export of parts. The specification stays public.

## 9. Governance and operations
A central body (a federal agency, per v1.0) sets the specification. Provincial and municipal partners site the units. Public dashboards report cost, vacancy, energy and compute hours, and there is an annual public audit. v1.1 added "or a co-op federation" as an alternative. That alternative is noted here, but it was not hers.

## 10. Economic analysis (first principles)

### 10.1 Method
Material cost = quantity (from geometry) × dated unit price. Labour = hours × the Ontario carpenter median wage of ${{jobbank.wage}}/h [JobBank]. Energy value = kWh × tariff. Take-off rules for the reference unit:
- **Studs per wall:** ceil(L × 12 / {{unit.spacing_in}}) + {{rule.end_studs}}, plus {{rule.corner_studs}} per corner (L in ft, 12 in/ft).
- **Plates:** {{rule.plate_runs}} × perimeter, cut from {{lumber.length_ft}} ft pieces.
- **OSB:** walls + roof deck + subfloor.
- **R22 batts:** walls + roof + floor.
- **Drywall:** wall interiors + ceiling.
- No deduction for openings.

Unit prices are Kent.ca retail, accessed {{kent.date}}, pre-tax [Kent]. Lumber carbon uses CWC EPD 845, Table 7 (Ontario, A1–A3 = {{cwc.gwp}} kg CO₂e/m³) [CWC-EPD]. The Chain column below is built from the same constants as the Value column.

### 10.3 Interpretation
- **The energy-only ROI {{concl.fails}} at every OEB price.** A {{roi.long}}-year energy-only payback on a ${{cost.low_k}}k unit needs ${{e11.tariff}}/kWh, which {{cmp.e11_top.exceeds}} OEB's highest price ({{oeb.ulo_peak_cents}} ¢/kWh, ULO on-peak) by a factor of {{e12.ratio}} (E11–E12). The {{roi.long}}-year unit-cost ceiling runs from ${{e7.ceiling}} at Tier 1 to ${{e10.ceiling}} at ULO on-peak (E7–E10). The partial-shell materials (B5, ${{b5.material}}) are only part of the unit cost, which is not yet derived, so they do not settle the question on their own.
- The partial shell (B5) is a small fraction of the ${{cost.low_k}}–{{cost.high_k}}k target. The rest of the cost sits in items not yet derived: roof and floor structure, roofing, windows, doors, foundation, wet core, electrical, mechanical, ramp, finishes, permits, land and site work. Until those are taken off, **the ${{cost.low_k}}–{{cost.high_k}}k unit cost is unverified**.
- Labour hours for a {{unit.sqft}} sq ft unit have no primary source yet. L1–L3 are sensitivity points only.
- Energy pays the occupant about ${{e2.offset_whole}}/yr in offsets at Tier 1, and up to about ${{e2.offset_ulo_whole}}/yr if every kWh offset ULO on-peak consumption (E7–E10 prices), not the public in cash. Revenue-positive therefore depends on avoided public costs (unsourced, L4) or a change in export rules.
- R22 in the roof and floor is a placeholder. Insulation must meet the energy-efficiency requirements of the code in force.

### 10.4 Benefit-cost framework
The public-finance case is avoided costs: shelter, health and emergency services. v1.0 stated $10–20B. No source has been found, so the figure is not used.

## 11. Risk management

| Class | Failure | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Economic | Cost overrun | Open-book BOMs; regenerate the model on every price change |
| Social / political | Inequity, siting opposition | Community siting; disability and income audits |
| Technical | Interface drift | Frozen spec against ICC/MBI 1200/1205/1210 and CSA A277 certification |
| Environmental | Construction waste, embodied carbon | Lifecycle assessment per EPD; take-back |
| Legal / privacy | Abuse of compute nodes | PIPEDA; no default cameras; deletion logs |
| Corruption | Procurement graft | Open contracting [OCDS], blockchain tracking [WEF-2020], beneficial-ownership registries, whistleblower protection (OECD / UNCAC [UNCAC]) |

## 12. Testing, validation and evaluation
This paper, the README and CLAIMS.md are rendered from `model/templates/` by `cargo run -q -p choam-model -- --write`. `cargo test` (from a clean clone) checks:
1. Every derivation behaves as specified, and invalid inputs are rejected.
2. Each committed document is byte-identical to a fresh render, so any hand edit to a model-derived number anywhere in it (prose, tables or the generated block) fails.
3. Every other number in the templates is on `model/numbers-allowlist.tsv` with its location (a line context), its kind (source quote, Ashlynn's figure, identifier or date) and its source; a number that is neither generated nor allowlisted fails, and an allowlisted quote may not equal a model-derived value.

CI runs fmt, clippy (pedantic, warnings denied), the tests (including doctests), `cargo audit` and `cargo deny`. Pilot metrics are listed in section 8, and a third-party audit comes before scale-up.

## 13. Prior work
- **Universal Basic Services**, including shelter, free at the point of need [UBS-2017]. CHOAM is a concrete shelter specification for that idea.
- **Right to housing.** Canada's National Housing Strategy Act [NHSA-2019].
- **Off-site construction economics.** Terner Center 2017 (multifamily: savings of up to 20% on the cost of construction, 40–50% time) [Terner-2017]; McKinsey 2019 (20–50% schedule, more than 20% cost at scale, 2D vs 3D logistics) [McKinsey-2019].
- **Open housing hardware.** WikiHouse [WikiHouse]; CERN OHL [CERN-OHL].
- **Volunteer computing.** BOINC [BOINC]; Folding@home [FAH].
- **Procurement transparency.** WEF/IDB blockchain procurement pilot (Colombia) [WEF-2020]; Open Contracting Data Standard [OCDS].
- **Codes.** ICC/MBI off-site standards [ICC-MBI]; CSA A277 [CHBA-A277]; NBC 2020 [NBC-2020]; 2024 OBC [OBC-2024].

## 14. Limitations
- **L1.** The BOM covers four material lines only (B1–B4), at one Atlantic-Canada retailer's prices, pre-tax, without delivery or volume discounts. Ontario prices may differ.
- **L2.** The labour hours are not sourced. The wage is a 2023–2024 reference-period median that we read through a search index, because jobbank.gc.ca refused a direct fetch.
- **L3.** The energy figures use NRCan's municipal model for Toronto at latitude tilt. They are not a site simulation, and shading, snow and orientation will lower them. Tier-1 is the commodity price only; whether net-metering credits offset other volumetric charges depends on the utility. The unit's consumption is unsourced, so the Tier-1 bill offsets are an assumption; rows E7–E10 show the effect of OEB's other prices.
- **L4.** The avoided public costs needed for "revenue-positive" have not been sourced.
- **L5.** The code-compliance statements cite the codes' scope and certification route. They are not a code review of a design, because no drawings exist yet. The stud table was read through NRC's reproduction of the NBC 2020 first printing [NRC-PCF-1677]; the NBC 2020 PDF itself could not be fetched from the audit box, and the second printing (2025 errata) was not checked.
- **L6.** The construction-speed and cost literature is US multifamily evidence and may not transfer to {{unit.sqft}} sq ft single-storey units.
- **L7.** Embodied carbon covers the lumber only (fossil, A1–A3). OSB, insulation and gypsum EPDs have not been applied.

- **Deleted as unsourced numbers:**
  - $500–600/sq ft
  - $1–2B factories
  - 16 weeks/unit
  - $200–500/unit/yr net metering
  - $1–3B solar
  - $1B compute
  - $10–20B savings
  - 36-inch clearances (added in v1.1)

- **Flagged:**
